# Ethereum Classic DAO

> Building the software and infrastructure for global adoption of Ethereum Classic — the largest Proof-of-Work smart contract platform. Wyoming DAO LLC ensuring US regulatory compliance.

## About

Ethereum Classic DAO LLC is the legal entity for the Olympia DAO under Wyoming's DAO LLC framework (Filing ID 2025-001671865). The LLC builds software, ecosystem infrastructure, and hashrate incentives for the world's largest Proof-of-Work smart contract platform — while ensuring proper reporting and compliance with US federal and state regulatory frameworks.

Ethereum Classic (ETC) is the only Proof-of-Work blockchain with native EVM smart contracts. Every Ethereum framework, library, and IDE works with Ethereum Classic — just change the chain ID (61 mainnet, 63 Mordor testnet). Network upgrades are coordinated to maintain EVM protocol parity, delivering a best-in-class EVM experience.

ETC is positioned not just as a digital commodity under the CLARITY Act, but as a compliant smart contract platform where regulated stablecoins (GENIUS Act) and ETF-aligned ERC-20 tokens can operate on a Proof-of-Work foundation.

## Legal Structure

- **Entity:** Ethereum Classic DAO LLC
- **Jurisdiction:** Wyoming, United States
- **Filing ID:** 2025-001671865
- **Framework:** Wyoming Decentralized Autonomous Organization Supplement
- **Registered Agent:** 30 N Gould St Ste R, Sheridan, WY 82801
- **Regulatory alignment:** CLARITY Act (digital commodity), GENIUS Act (stablecoins on EVM)

## Olympia — Ethereum Classic's Most Significant Protocol Upgrade

The Olympia era marks a shift from reactive maintenance to active development on the longest-running EVM and the only Proof-of-Work smart contract platform in the world. Three client-facing ECIPs form the core of the upgrade:

**ECIP-1111 — EIP-1559 Fee Market:** Adds the most widely adopted transaction format in the EVM ecosystem to Ethereum Classic. Dynamic gas pricing delivers predictable fees for users and applications. Fully additive — legacy transactions remain valid indefinitely. Unlike Ethereum where the basefee is burned, ETC redirects it to the protocol treasury. Miner block rewards and tips remain completely untouched.

**ECIP-1112 — Protocol Treasury:** A protocol-controlled vault funded by basefee revenue and voluntary contributions. For the first time, institutions, developers, and network stakeholders can directly fund Ethereum Classic's core development and critical infrastructure without fielding their own team. Only on-chain governance can release funds — no admin keys, no multisig.

**ECIP-1121 — Fusaka EVM Alignment:** Advances ETC's execution layer through London, Dencun, Pectra, and Fusaka in a single upgrade — ending Ethereum Classic's longest period of EVM stagnation. Exchanges and wallets gain modern RPC compatibility and standard transaction support. Developers gain full access to every current Ethereum tool, library, and framework without modification.

**Governance Process:**
1. Propose — Community members submit governance proposals on-chain (permissionless)
2. Vote — Olympia membership NFT holders cast weighted on-chain votes
3. Queue — Approved proposals enter a security timelock
4. Execute — After timelock, proposals execute automatically on-chain
5. Disclose — All outcomes publicly reported and verifiable

**Safeguards:** Configurable timelock, three-layer on-chain sanctions screening, non-transferable membership NFT voting tokens.

**Institutional Positioning:** Ethereum Classic is the Proof-of-Work infrastructure layer for institutions and sovereign nations building compliant financial systems — regulated stablecoins under MiCA and the GENIUS Act, energy grid stabilization backed by immutable settlement, and ETF-compliant digital asset infrastructure that regulators across the US, EU, Japan, and beyond are moving to define.

## Network Statistics

- Hashrate: 170+ TH/s (largest PoW smart contract network, absorbed Ethereum mining infrastructure post-Merge)
- Markets: 300+ active markets across 20+ major global exchanges
- Independent clients: fukuii (Scala, primary), core-geth (Go), besu (Java)
- Network origin: July 30, 2015 (genesis block — oldest EVM-compatible blockchain)
- Chain IDs: 61 (mainnet), 63 (Mordor testnet)

## Client Implementations

Three independent implementations ensure zero single points of failure:
- **fukuii** — Purpose-built for Ethereum Classic. Independent implementation designed for performance, security, and protocol parity. Primary client for the Olympia upgrade.
- **core-geth** — The longest-running ETC client, forked from go-ethereum. Battle-tested stability across every network upgrade since genesis.
- **besu** — Enterprise-grade client built on Hyperledger Besu. Cross-client protocol verification and consensus compatibility validation.

## Developer Tooling (Full EVM Compatibility)

- Smart Contract Development: Hardhat, Foundry (forge/cast/anvil), Remix IDE, OpenZeppelin Contracts 5.x
- Client Libraries: ethers.js v6, viem, web3.js v4
- Wallets: 50+ wallet integrations including hardware wallets, browser extensions, and mobile wallets
- Infrastructure: Public RPC endpoints, block explorers, oracle networks
- Security: Slither, Mythril, Echidna

- Grayscale Ethereum Classic Trust (ETCG) — regulated securities exposure since 2017, ETF conversion pipeline in progress
- Institutional-grade digital asset custody from leading custodians
- 300+ active markets across 20+ major global exchanges and retail brokerages worldwide

## Olympia Upgrade Guide

Node operators must upgrade before the Olympia activation block. Three clients available:

- **Fukuii** (Scala, JDK 21+) — Primary client post-Olympia. 143 RPC methods, 2,706 tests.
- **Core-Geth** (Go 1.24+) — Transitioning to maintenance role.
- **Hyperledger Besu** (Java 21+) — Enterprise-grade, Apache 2.0 licensed.

Prerequisites: 8 GB RAM, 500 GB SSD. Block rewards and tips remain untouched — only EIP-1559 basefee is redirected to the treasury.

## Olympia Development Timeline

Six phases from specification to mainnet:

1. Specification Drafting (2024 Q3 – 2025 Q2) — Complete. Three client-facing ECIPs: ECIP-1111 (EIP-1559 fee market), ECIP-1112 (treasury contract), ECIP-1121 (Fusaka EVM alignment). Plus contract layer ECIPs 1113 and 1114.
2. Client Implementation (2025 Q1 – 2025 Q4) — Complete. Three independent implementations.
3. Governance Contracts (2025 Q3 – 2026 Q1) — Complete. Demo v0.3 deployed (9 contracts).
4. Testnet Deployment (2026 Q1 – present) — In progress. Mordor sync verified, SNAP sync successful.
5. Olympia Upgrade core developers call — Upcoming. Activation block to be announced.
6. Mainnet Activation — Upcoming. EIP-1559 basefee begins flowing to treasury.
